$comment: Fixed points with seeded placement, GAME_DESIGN.md section 9. Hollowbrook is always at the origin. The Hall and the standing stones are placed at seeded angles inside a distance band, always on ground flat enough to build on. Landmarks.ts searches the band with the world RNG and never calls Math.random.

village.name: Hollowbrook
village.$comment: Terrain.ts already flattens a plateau here, so no search is needed.
village.$comment_walls: Spacing between wall-ring collider spheres, Structures.ts. A house wall run is only 6-9m, so a coarse step (the old 1.4, radius 1.05) pulled the walkable interior in by more than a metre a side once the player's own capsule radius is added at test time. 0.5 (radius 0.375) still overlaps along a straight run with room to spare (WallRing.pushRun's 0.75x-of-step multiplier only needs step/2 of overlap), so the wall stays solid; it just costs more, cheap, colliders to trace the same footprint.
village.$comment_houseClearingMargin: Clearings.ts: metres added past each house's own half-diagonal (from villageHousePlacements' placeholder width/depth) when it suppresses scatter around that one building. Covers the real loaded model, which can run a little larger than the placeholder box, and the doorway apron so nothing sprouts on the threshold.
village.$comment_home: House index 0's furniture, marking it as the player's home for the wake-up scene a later milestone spawns into. Offsets are local to that house's own frame (front at -z, same convention as the door anchors in models.json). house_a's own wall plane sits at half-extent 3.0 (models.json's door.z), so floor/table/chair/bookcase/rug all stay inside +-2.8 to clear the walls.

home.$comment_floor: Widened to cover the room's real 6x6m interior (was 4.2x5.2, offset toward the back wall only: bare ground showed at the door and past both side walls). Centred on the house's own origin now, per D62.
home.$comment_furniture: Kenney Furniture Kit pieces (models.json's homeFurniture), added per D62 so the room reads as lived-in: a nightstand for the lamp, a chair, a bookcase against the side wall, a rug underfoot. Each falls back to nothing (or, for table/lamp, the old primitives) if its model fails to load; furnishHome() in Structures.ts does the placing.
home.$comment_lamp: The one light this scene is allowed (a handheld target keeps it to one, src/core/babylon.ts's PointLight). x/z match `table` above, since the lamp model stands ON the table now instead of floating unsupported at y=1.3; `y` is the light source's own height (table height plus roughly the lamp shade's own), not the model's mount height (models.json's homeFurniture.table.height). `radius` sizes the emissive-cylinder fallback if the real lamp model fails to load.
home.$comment_orinOffset: Where Grandpa Orin waits at a fresh spawn (Structures.pointNear, forward/side local to the house frame), clear of the player's own spawn point at the room's centre. There is no NPC movement system (src/entities/NPC.ts has no per-frame update), so this is where he stands rather than where he walks in from.

hall.name: The Meadows Hall
hall.$comment: The building is axis-aligned to its own yaw. Interior is one room, entry at -z, Bracken at +z, four alcoves down the long walls.
hall.$road: The road stub points back toward the village so a player who finds the Hall from any direction has a thread to follow home, and a player following the road from the village arrives at the door.

$search: Both searched landmarks sample candidate angles from the seeded RNG and take the first that clears maxSlope and sits above the waterline. If no candidate in `attempts` qualifies, the flattest seen wins, so world generation always terminates with a placement.
$comment_playerRadius: The character capsule's radius (src/entities/CharacterController.ts DEFAULT_CONFIG.radius), duplicated here because that file is TypeScript, not a data file, and is off limits this session (another pass owns src/core/input, HUD, DialoguePanel and Story). WallRing.ts's door-gap maths needs it to size a walkable slot the controller actually agrees is walkable; a future pass should have CharacterController read this value instead of the reverse.
